findings.title: Worker queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure and memory can grow without limit
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates plain queue.Queue() instances with no maxsize. The class docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but an unbounded queue never blocks the consumer's submit path, so the Kafka consumer thread will keep polling and enqueueing WorkItems (each holding the full decoded result and original message) as fast as it can read them. If one group/queue is slow (the exact problem this PR is meant to mitigate), items pile up in memory instead of applying backpressure via the consumer, risking OOM of the consumer pod and defeating offset-based flow control. The queues should have a bounded maxsize so submit() blocks and arroyo stops polling.

findings.title: Worker commits offsets for messages whose processing raised an exception
findings.body: In OrderedQueueWorker.run, the broad `except Exception` only logs, and the `finally` block unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset(). That means a work item whose result_processor raised is marked complete and its offset becomes committable, so the message is silently dropped rather than redelivered or sent to a DLQ. This contradicts the strategy docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'. Today ResultProcessor.__call__ swallows its own exceptions so this path is rarely hit, but any exception thrown outside that wrapper (e.g. in sentry_sdk transaction handling or a future processor) causes permanent message loss with only a log line. Failed items should either not complete the offset (forcing redelivery) or be routed to the DLQ.

findings.title: No handling of partition revocation; stale offsets keep being committed after rebalance
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy starts a background commit thread that commits whatever OffsetTracker considers committable, but nothing in the strategy or in ResultsStrategyFactory resets state when partitions are revoked during a rebalance. After a rebalance the OffsetTracker still holds entries for partitions this consumer no longer owns, and the commit thread will happily commit those offsets to the consumer group, potentially clobbering progress made by the new owner of the partition. Additionally, if the factory's create_with_partitions is called again for a new assignment, a second commit thread is spawned while the old pool/tracker state lingers. Partition revocation should clear tracker state for revoked partitions and stop committing them.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling is flaky and its assertion contradicts the implementation
findings.body: The test mocks the result processor to raise on the first call, then asserts no offsets were committed. But OrderedQueueWorker completes offsets in a finally block even when processing raises, so offset 100 becomes committable immediately and the 1-second commit loop will commit offset 101/102 for the partition. The test only passes because it breaks out of the wait loop after ~0.2s, racing the commit thread's 1.0s interval — under load or on a slow CI runner the commit can land before the assertion, making the test fail nondeterministically. Either the implementation should not commit failed offsets, or the test should assert the actual (committed-past-failure) behavior deterministically.
